cross_cultural.reason: Level 3: current, specific inclusion activities with reported figures. These are an employee resource group with a membership figure (nearly 100 members, E1), the Dignity of Work sourcing pledge benefiting refugees and people with disabilities (over 300 and over 500 hours, E5), and a resort Hawaiian cultural center connecting visitors and the local community (five full-time Native Hawaiian staff, E10). Further current activities without figures support this (E2-E4, E6-E9). Not level 4, because cross-cultural access is not a major part of the lodging REIT business. The 10-K alone gives demographics only (E11).

ai.notes: The 10-K gives only workforce demographics and points to the separate Corporate Responsibility Report, so this rescore relies mainly on the report. Several figures are small in absolute terms because Host has only about 163 employees. WIN is open to all employees and is women-focused. The 3 rests on the rubric's explicit example (an employee network with membership figures) plus multiple other activities with figures; a stricter reading of 'several small activities' could argue for 2. Items excluded or not counted: the Sunflower Bakery partnership at Gaithersburg is described as a pilot and was not cited. The Dreyfus BOLD/GRACE investment was excluded because the donations are made by Dreyfus, not Host, and the social impact funds also cover non-inclusion aims. Hotel-manager inclusion 'best practices' (recruiting veterans and refugees) are general and not specific to Host. The 2030 supplier and inclusion targets are planned. The pay equity study was a past activity. ADA accessibility is legal compliance and was not scored.
